cohort: The study included 51 women who experienced obstetric anal sphincter injuries (OASIS) after vaginal delivery.
finding: Primiparity, delivery duration longer than 10 hours, and episiotomy use were identified as risk factors for obstetric anal sphincter injuries (OASIS).
mod_finding: Episiotomy use was associated with a higher prevalence of OASIS compared to no episiotomy.
birth_weight: neonatal birth weight was measured, but no specific weight was mentioned
